title: Early Inflection
method: Looks for stocks in an 'early LITE-2025' position: revenue that has bottomed and is accelerating, rising margins, strong forward growth and a reasonable price, before the stock has already run. Universe: every US-listed stock with a $1B–$30B market cap on Nasdaq's screener (excluding banks, insurers, REITs and other financials), then 3+ analysts with a price target, $100M+ TTM revenue and $5M+ a day of trading, with revenue growing in the latest quarter and 8%+ implied growth over the next 12 months. Each survivor is scored 0–100 on the rubric below; the top 12 are the picks and the next 18 form the ranked bench, with at most 3 per industry. Excludes bitcoin/crypto miners, other commodity producers (metal, coal and lithium miners, oil & gas producers, refiners, smelters, fertilizer makers: their revenue tracks commodity prices) and pending-merger targets. Revenue points are halved when growth looks bought (a big jump in goodwill/intangibles or share count).
pattern: Lumentum (LITE) bottomed at $49.56 on Apr 4, 2025 and closed 2025 at $368.59 (+644%); by Oct 2026 it was about 22x the low. What was visible at the time: revenue had troughed in mid-2024 and was accelerating (+6%, +10%, +16% YoY), gross margin had risen four quarters in a row, it beat the top of guidance and then raised mid-quarter, it supplied a bottleneck (laser chips for AI optics; Nvidia's co-packaged-optics partner), and it traded near 2.3x sales and ~17x forward earnings after a tariff-driven 48% drop while analysts were cutting targets. The stock reclaimed its 200-day average a week after the May beat-and-raise and broke its 2021 high in late July 2025, and buying that breakout still returned about 10x. This screen scores today's stocks on the same signals. Hindsight caveat: no one knew in 2025 how big the move would be, and most stocks that pass a screen like this will not become LITE.

rubric.how: Latest-quarter YoY growth vs the prior quarter (up to 7) and vs a year earlier (up to 7), plus the growth level (up to 6, full at 40%+). Zero if revenue is shrinking.
Gross margin (last 2 quarters vs same 2 a year earlier, full at +5 pts) up to 9; operating margin (full at +8 pts) up to 6.
Implied next-12-month revenue growth (P/S ÷ forward P/S, full at 35%+) up to 10; 3-yr EPS growth forecast (full at 40%+) up to 5.
Forward P/E (15 or less full, 45+ zero) up to 9; EV / forward sales (2x or less full, 10x+ zero) up to 6.
1-yr move up to +100% scores 7, fading to 5 at +150% and 1 at +300%; over +300% scores 0 and costs 5 more points. Plus up to 3 for a 15–50% pullback from the 52-week high.
Above the 200-day average 4, above the 50-day 2, 50-day above 200-day 2, beating SPY over 3 months 2.
Upside to the average target (full at 50%+) up to 6; consensus Strong Buy 4, Buy 3, Hold 1.

AI-infrastructure supplier industries (semis, chip equipment, optics/communication equipment, electronic components, hardware, electrical equipment) 5; adjacent industries (instruments, industrial machinery, power producers, engineering & construction) 3.

dataNotes: Prices are Nasdaq closes (2026-10-22). Quarterly revenue and margins come from StockAnalysis income statements (S&P Global Market Intelligence); forward P/E, P/S, forward P/S, EV/sales, EPS growth forecast, 50/200-day averages, consensus rating, analyst count and average target come from StockAnalysis statistics pages. Next-12-month revenue growth is implied as P/S ÷ forward P/S. Beat-and-raise history is not scored automatically. Analyst target and forward P/S are saved daily (data/early-inflection-history.json), so 30-day revisions show up from early November 2026. This run: 1422 names screened, 1196 passed the filters, 517 scored on fundamentals, top 70 checked against price history. 'n/a' means not available.

disclaimer: Early-stage ideas for research only. Inflections can fail, cyclical recoveries can reverse, and most stocks that pass this screen will not become the next LITE. Not financial advice.

KLIC.text: Fiscal Q3 (Jun 2026) revenue $330.4M, +123% YoY, back to a GAAP profit. Guided fiscal Q4 (ended Oct 3) to $375M ±$20M at ~48% gross margin; that report is due in November.

TTMI.text: Q2 2026 sales a record $1.0B (+37% YoY), above the $930–970M guide; book-to-bill 1.49; Data Center & Networking 40% of sales. Q3 guide $1.10–1.14B; full-year 2026 raised to about $4.4B (excludes pending acquisitions).

UCTT.text: Q2 2026 revenue a record $644.9M (vs $533.7M in Q1), back to a GAAP profit. Q3 guide $700–750M; adding capacity for a ~$4B annual revenue run rate by mid-2027.

AEIS.text: Q2 2026 data-center computing revenue $191.5M (+35% YoY); raised its 2026 data-center growth outlook to 50%+ and guided Q3 revenue to $640M ±$20M.

SIMO.text: Q3 2026 results due after the close on Oct 28 (call Oct 29). In Q2 it beat estimates with $451M revenue and $2.43 EPS, and the stock rose 7.7% on the report.

SITM.text: Guided Q3 revenue to $285M–$295M (about $85M from the acquired Renesas timing business) and non-GAAP EPS of $3.50–$3.65; Morgan Stanley started coverage at Overweight with a $730 target and Needham raised its target to $900.

URGN.text: ZUSDURI launch is gaining speed: Q2 revenue $50.4M (+73% QoQ), 450 prescribers and 45% repeat writers. UGN-103's NDA is filed, with a PDUFA date expected in June 2027.

SMCI.text: FY2026 revenue $39.1B; guided FY2027 revenue to $65B–$72B on a record backlog. Risk: a co-founder was charged in an alleged chip-export case (Supermicro says it is not a defendant).

HLIT.text: At its Sept 15 Investor Day, Harmonic reaffirmed 2026 revenue guidance of $505M–$525M (about +43% YoY) and targets 20%+ operating margins; it also launched the Comcast-developed Recon fiber-monitoring products.

NESR.text: Record Q2: revenue $520.8M (+59% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA $106.2M; won about $300M of multiyear Kuwait well-testing and technology work, with the Jafurah gas ramp expected to lift Q3.

LSCC.text: Record Q2 revenue $201.1M (+62% YoY); Q3 guide $245M–$265M includes two months of the AMI acquisition (part of the jump is acquired). Launched the Mach-N2 secure-control FPGA family on Sept 16.

TVTX.text: FILSPARI's FSGS launch is ramping (2,012 patient start forms) and a new patent allowance should extend US coverage to Oct 2037; CEO Eric Dube hands over to Bradley Campbell on Dec 1.

TLN.text: Upsized its buyback to $3.0B through 2028 with $1.5B of accelerated repurchases, funded by monetizing ~$1.5B of future PJM capacity revenue; projects ~$4B adjusted FCF from 2H26 through 2028. President Terry Nutt becomes CEO on Jan 1, 2027. The stock jumped ~9.7% intraday on Oct 6.

KMT.text: Fiscal Q4 (Jun 2026) sales $737M, +43% YoY (42% organic), on pricing in an "unprecedented tungsten environment"; record adjusted EPS $2.96. FY27 guide: sales $3.33B–$3.45B (vs $2.36B in FY26), adjusted EPS $4.15–$5.15. Risk: much of the margin jump is raw-material pricing timing (~$252M in Q4), and FY26 free operating cash flow was −$79M on tungsten inventory.

UGP.text: 2Q26: Ipiranga's recurring adjusted EBITDA was R$2.78B (+310% YoY) at R$451/m³ vs R$118 a year earlier; group recurring adjusted EBITDA R$3.7B, net income R$1.7B and record R$4.8B operating cash generation. Figures are in Brazilian reais; fuel-distribution margins are volatile.

PENG.text: Fiscal Q4 (Aug 2026) net sales a record $567M (+68% YoY), with growth accelerating from 48% in Q3; raised its fiscal 2027 outlook to about $2.43B in net sales (+40% ±10 pts) and $4.45 non-GAAP EPS on neocloud AI-infrastructure wins.

COHU.text: Q2 2026 net sales $149.0M (+38% YoY), test-cell utilization up to about 80%; raised its 2026 high-performance-computing revenue estimate to $100M–$110M and guided Q3 sales to $170M ±$7M.

DHT.text: Q3 2026 fleet TCE estimated at $141,300/day (spot VLCCs $167,100/day) vs $126,700/day in Q2; about 50% of Q4 spot days already booked at $509,100/day, with ~78% of all Q4 revenue days at $225,200/day (Oct 14 business update). Crude-tanker earnings are rate-cyclical.

VICR.text: Q2 2026 revenue $143.4M (+27% QoQ; royalties $30.4M vs $10.4M a year ago); backlog $380M, +26% QoQ and +145% YoY, as AI/high-performance-compute demand fills its first ChiP fab and it plans a second fab for 2nd Gen VPD.
